claim_text: Microsoft puts the outage window at 4:20 PM UTC on Thursday, Nov 12 (11:20 AM ET) to 4:10 PM UTC on Friday, Nov 13 (11:10 AM ET), under incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821.
label: Confirmed
source_name: Microsoft Preliminary Post Incident Report EX1550543/MO1550821 (third-party copy hosted by opensecurity.es)
why_it_supports: Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report gives these incident start and end times.
notes: Third-party copies: Microsoft's own copy of the report needs a Microsoft 365 admin-center login (not checked: login required). The university mirror shows the same end time in Microsoft's final status text, but its record header lists a 10:05 AM UTC start for EX1550543; we use the report's 4:20 PM UTC. corroborated_by: https://mailservices.isc.upenn.edu/computing/email/penno365/alerts/ms-incidents.html corroborated_by: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-says-months-old-bug-caused-global-microsoft-365-outage/

claim_text: Microsoft first posted about Teams problems in North America at 10:40 AM ET on Nov 12, and about Exchange Online mailbox access problems in the Americas at 12:54 PM ET.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Microsoft's official status account posted the Teams investigation notice at this time.

claim_text: Exchange Online took the main hit: most users could not reach their mailboxes through Outlook or other mail apps, and email delivery was delayed. Parts of Copilot, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Defender and Purview that rely on Exchange Online were also affected.
label: Confirmed
source_name: Microsoft Preliminary Post Incident Report EX1550543/MO1550821 (third-party copy hosted by opensecurity.es)
why_it_supports: The report's User Impact section describes the primary and secondary impact in these terms.
notes: Third-party copy of Microsoft's report; see c001. corroborated_by: https://www.securityweek.com/microsoft-rules-out-cyberattack-in-outage-warns-of-phishing-campaign/

claim_text: Users in at least 70 countries reported problems.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: BBC News reports Microsoft's email, Teams and Copilot were inaccessible in at least 70 countries.
notes: Based on outage-tracker reports. AP reported more than 70 countries from Downdetector data, but its page blocked our check.

claim_text: According to Microsoft's preliminary report, three things together caused the outage: a latent defect in a July update made for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers, extra load after Teams failed over to the same gateway about 15 hours earlier, and nearly 14% of gateway capacity already out of service for an unrelated reason.
label: Confirmed
source_name: Microsoft Preliminary Post Incident Report EX1550543/MO1550821 (third-party copy hosted by opensecurity.es)
why_it_supports: The report's Root Cause section lists these three factors.
notes: This is Microsoft's own analysis. The final report, due Nov 20, may add to or change it. A Microsoft executive vice president posted a public summary of the same findings on X, reported by ABC News and The Verge. corroborated_by: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-says-months-old-bug-caused-global-microsoft-365-outage/ corroborated_by: https://www.theregister.com/saas/2026/11/16/microsoft-blames-monster-email-outage-on-software-defect-introduced-in-july-fix/5310026 corroborated_by: https://www.theverge.com/tech/1035364/microsoft-outlook-outage-notepad

claim_text: Microsoft's preliminary report says more than 80% of the gateway servers were unresponsive at the lowest point, and that safeguards between regions did not stop the failure from spreading worldwide.
label: Confirmed
source_name: Microsoft Preliminary Post Incident Report EX1550543/MO1550821 (third-party copy hosted by opensecurity.es)
why_it_supports: The report states both points in its Root Cause section.

claim_text: Microsoft said the outage was "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents", introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced by a recent network change.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Microsoft's official X account posted this statement on Nov 13.
notes: Microsoft also sent the statement to BBC News, and it appears in the final status text of both incidents. corroborated_by: https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cq5y10ge3dp3t

claim_text: During the outage, Microsoft's status updates said there was no indication or evidence of malicious or cyber activity.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Microsoft's official status account said there was no indication the outage was the result of malicious or cyber activity.

claim_text: Microsoft engineers looked into possible attack routes, consulted DDoS specialists, and ruled out an attack using crash reports and logs.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Verge reports this from sources familiar with the response.

claim_text: The Microsoft 365 outage was caused by a cyberattack, hack or DDoS.
label: Debunked
why_it_supports: The White House quotes the Director of National Intelligence saying the recent outages are not a cyberattack, and the Secretary of State saying there is zero evidence any of them involve hackers or hostile actors and that the Microsoft incident is unrelated to the FAA's.
notes: Also contradicted by Microsoft (c007, c008). No independent forensic report has been published; this label will be revisited if new official findings appear. corroborated_by: https://x.com/i/status/2121282013600907325

claim_text: The outage was caused by AI-written code or AI agents.
label: Rumor
why_it_supports: The Verge reports people outside Microsoft wondering whether the outage came from a cyberattack or careless AI coding.
notes: Microsoft says the outage was not related to AI or agents (c007), and its preliminary report blames a July fix without saying how it was written. Not labeled Debunked because only Microsoft has addressed it.

claim_text: The Microsoft outage was part of a coordinated attack linked to the FAA, bank and other outages that week.
label: Debunked
why_it_supports: The White House says officials see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity or malign actor, and the Secretary of State says the Microsoft incident has nothing to do with the FAA's.
notes: This is the US government's account, not an independent technical analysis. NBC News also reports security researchers saying the simpler explanation is brittle systems. corroborated_by: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crkgvxxwpwz2o

claim_text: Criminals sent phishing emails posing as Microsoft 365 outage notices that cited the real incident ID EX1550543 and falsely warned that held mail would be deleted. Microsoft says stolen credentials and malware have not been confirmed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes the campaign, its subject lines and sender domains.
notes: This was a separate, opportunistic scam that exploited the outage. It did not cause the outage. corroborated_by: https://www.securityweek.com/microsoft-rules-out-cyberattack-in-outage-warns-of-phishing-campaign/

claim_text: Microsoft extended its email timeout to 48 hours so that mail delayed during the outage would not be returned as undeliverable.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Microsoft's official status account posted the 48-hour extension.

claim_text: Microsoft released a preliminary post-incident report on Nov 15 to 16, available only inside the Microsoft 365 admin center.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Microsoft's official status account said the preliminary report was available in the admin center under MO1550821 and EX1550543.
notes: We did not log in to read it. The text we cite is a third-party copy (c001).

claim_text: Microsoft says its final post-incident report is due Nov 20, 2026.
label: Confirmed
source_name: Microsoft Preliminary Post Incident Report EX1550543/MO1550821 (third-party copy hosted by opensecurity.es)
why_it_supports: The preliminary report's repair-items table lists the full list of repair items as due 11/20/2026 with the final report.

claim_text: On Nov 18, Microsoft's Azure status page showed no active events, and Azure's status history listed no incident review newer than Sep 30, 2026.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Azure status page read "There are currently no active events" when we checked.

claim_text: A major Microsoft Azure outage happened on Nov 18, 2026.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Microsoft's Azure status page showed no active events, and we found no outlet reporting a major Azure outage that day.
notes: Third-party outage trackers showed only scattered user reports on Nov 18. The Microsoft outage people discussed that week was this Nov 12 to 13 Microsoft 365 outage.
